title: Handoff Tapestry: Weekly SRE Weave
content:
Summary
---
This week focused on two small incidents (one partial degradation of hosted-chat, one autoscaler misfiring in Dedicated), an SLO post-mortem draft, and a set of runbook edits to make handoffs less noisy. Handoff experiment (see section below) ran for 48 hours and reduced duplicate pages by approx. 25%.

Incidents (concise)
1) 2027-04-18 03:12 UTC — hosted-chat tokenization error (partial degrade)
   - Impact: ~3% of chat requests returned tokenization exception for 7 minutes; errors routed to fallback model causing increased latency (~120ms tail). No data loss.
   - Symptoms: sudden spike in tokenizer exceptions, visible in error rate metric and error-trace sampling.
   - Initial triage: on-call noticed error-rate spike from telemetry alert (err-rate > 0.5% sustained for 2 mins). Pager to channel.
   - Root cause hypothesis: tokenizer upgrade (v2.14) deploy rolled out by canary at 03:05 which had an edge case for unusual unicode sequences.
   - Mitigation: rollback tokenizer to v2.13 at 03:18 by dev-deploy; errors dropped to baseline by 03:25.
   - Follow-ups: add a failing test case to tokenizer unit tests, update canary rollout gating (see action items). Jira: SRE-478.

2) 2027-04-19 14:07 UTC — Dedicated autoscaler misfire (burst scale-down overshoot)
   - Impact: 12-minute throughput dip for a small set of reserved pools (customer impact non-zero, one enterprise job throttled).
   - Symptoms: abrupt reduction of pod count, surge in queue length and rejected connections from load balancer.
   - Root cause: mis-evaluated spike-decay parameter in new autoscaler heuristic (merged in PR: ENGOPS-1023), combined with a timing race against eviction.
   - Mitigation: emergency patch to increase minimum-stabilization window + manual scale-up.
   - Follow-ups: revert PR for safety window, create canary for autoscaler heuristic changes, run synthetic load test for scale-down logic.

SLO / Metrics Snapshot
- Hosted API availability SLO (monthly): 99.95% target. Current reporting window (30d): 99.96%
- Chat latency P95 target: 200ms. Current 30d: 172ms. 7d: increased to 190ms during this week due to fallback routing from incident 1.
- Dedicated pool success rate (reserved pools): 99.8% target. Current weekly: 99.75% (dip during autoscaler event).
- Error rate trend: tokenizer exceptions caused +0.45% error bump for the 7-minute window.

Observed signals
- Alert noise: duplicate pages for the same incident were frequent across two channels. Experiment to centralize paging (handoff-tapestry protocol) reduced duplicates ~25% this week.
- Anomalies: small uptick in tail-latency from customers in eu-west1 region during autoscaler window — correlates with queued requests overflow.

Handoff notes (on-call to on-call)
- Outgoing (day shift -> evening shift 2027-04-20 17:00 UTC):
  - Keep an eye on tokenizer release cadence: any canary >1% traffic must stay pinned until smoke-tests pass for 30m.
  - Autoscaler: do not merge autoscaler heuristic PRs without a dedicated synthetic test run item attached to the PR.
  - Active tickets: SRE-478 (tokenizer test), ENGOPS-1023 (autoscaler revert + test plan).
  - Known degradations: None ongoing at handoff time.
- Incoming (evening -> night): ensure channel routing for page dedup (new filter deployed in pagerduty integration). If duplicate page appears, add "duplicate: true" tag in the incident Slack thread to help post-incident aggregation.

Runbook / Playbook edits (changes this week)
- Tokenizer rollback checklist: add step to validate synthetic unicode fixtures (added test fixture list).
- Autoscaler scale-down checklist: added minimum-stabilization-window flag and guidance for emergency manual scale-up.
- Paging filter: simple debounce logic implemented in pagerduty integration to suppress identical group pages within 90s window.

Action items (owners and ETA)
1) Priya: add failing unicode fixture + unit test to tokenizer repo. ETA: 2027-04-26. (linked SRE-478)
2) Marcus: prepare synthetic load harness for autoscaler scale-down tests; include burst and decay scenarios. ETA: 2027-05-03. (linked ENGOPS-1023)
3) Rafi: finalize post-incident writeup for tokenizer event and share in next ops review. ETA: 2027-04-23.
4) Ava: update canary gating doc and deploy checklist (small PR). ETA: 2027-04-25.
5) Oncall rotation team: observe pagerduty debounce for 2 weeks and report duplicate reduction metrics by 2027-05-04.

Retrospective notes (short)
- What went well: quick rollback path, clear alerting surfaced the spike early, collaboration between infra and tokenizer teams. Pager debounce experiment immediately reduced noise.
- What to improve: release gate needs more automated smoke coverage (synthetic traffic), autoscaler PRs need to attach test artifacts, clearer ticket ownership during cross-team handoffs.

Meeting items / Agenda for next SRE sync (2027-04-26)
- Review tokenizer post-incident writeup (Rafi)
- Autoscaler test harness demo (Marcus)
- Canary gating doc finalization (Ava)
- Handoff protocol: short review of tags and duplicate page strategy (10m)

Misc notes / scratchpad
- Quick metric snapshot table (raw):
  - hosted_chat_errors_1m: baseline 0.02% -> spike 0.47% (03:12-03:19 UTC 2027-04-18)
  - dedicated_pool_queue_length: baseline 5 -> peak 78 (14:07-14:19 UTC 2027-04-19)
  - p95_chat_latency_7d: 190ms -> p95_chat_latency_30d: 172ms
- Confluence links for runbook drafts: see linked artifacts above.
- Slack threads: #sre-ops (thread: "tokenizer-spike-2027-04-18"), #infra-deploys (thread: "autoscaler-misfire-2027-04-19").

Appendix: quick checklist for next on-call
- Verify pagerduty debounce is active (PD integration status page).
- If a tokenizer-related page surfaces, check the deploy dashboard for canary rate and roll-forward ID.
- Autoscaler alerts: if queue length grows >40 for >5 mins, alert SRE lead and trigger manual scale-up playbook.

End of note — short and practical. Add comments in the doc for anything I missed.
